new_statements.quote: [...] accented on its first syllable, or, if it is a monosyllable, on its only syllable. Within a phrase, i.e., a section of utterance between two secondary phonemes, the first or only syllable of the first word has primary stress accent, the first or only syllable of each succeeding word has secondary stress accent. All other syllables are unaccented. The primary stress accent is fairly strong, though not as strong as an English [...]; the secondary stress accent is less strong than the primary and frequently not too easily distinguishable from the primary stress or from lack of stress. The word is not otherwise phonemically marked; the beginnings and ends of words [...]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Every word is accented on its first syllable (a monosyllable on its only syllable). Within a phrase (the stretch between two junctures) the first word's first syllable carries primary stress and the first syllable of each following word carries secondary stress; all other syllables are unaccented. Stress is thus predictable and non-contrastive, and word boundaries are marked only by it.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress accent on the first syllable of every non-initial word of a phrase; weaker than the primary and often hard to distinguish from either primary stress or no stress. No rhythmic secondary stress within the word is mentioned.
new_statements.exceptions: Morphophonemic rules on pp. 18–19 refer to the accent: '3. In syllables with secondary accent or no accent, (a) ey > iy and ay > ey > iy, and, no matter what the accent, (b) iy >..'; '10. In an unaccented syllable a short vowel preceding r disappears'; and a noun 'in certain constructions.. loses its accent (becomes suffixal; the full word and the suffixal..)', i.e. an encliticized noun is unaccented.
new_statements.identity_note: Emeneau's Kota is the language of the Nilgiri Hills Kota villages (Kolme:l and others) recorded 1935–1938; no dialect split is stated in the passages read. Krishnamurti's book, if it discusses Kota stress, would be reporting Emeneau's data, not new fieldwork.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress on the first syllable; phrase-initial word gets primary, later words secondary stress; all other syllables unstressed.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Secondary stress on the first syllable of each non-initial word in a phrase; weaker and often indistinct.
new_statements.exceptions: Encliticized nouns lose their accent; several vowel rules (pp. 18–19) apply only in syllables with secondary or no accent.

audit.reasoning: Coding 'fixed-strict initial' (initial stress) rests on Emeneau 1944:16, a first-hand grammar sketch by the language's principal describer, and matches Gordon 2002 'Initial' and the StressTyp2 citation; nothing opened today (Subbaiah 1986, Rajasekaran 2008, LSI-TN 2023 Kota chapter) contradicts it — all are silent. But (a) we hold no file for the deciding passage: the verbatim quote exists only as snippet-stitched text from the earlier search and could not be re-verified today (HathiTrust/Google/IA/eScholarship all could not be reached by automated download), and (b) the one 344-pp reference grammar (Subbiah 1985) is unheld and unread. Hence 'thin' rather than at-risk: the source is authoritative for its era and the classification is typologically expected, but the quote is unconfirmable from disk.
